decisions.reason: This evening psychiatric day-patient program is closely aligned with the firm's existing psychiatric and psychosomatic expertise, so absorptive capacity is high and the firm is likely to refine rather than exit it.
The carpentry workshop draws on the firm's therapy and production know-how but is more commercially specialized than its core care services, so it is worth keeping with some moderate exit risk.
Outpatient sociotherapy fits the firm's established mental health and community-support capabilities, making it a product the firm can readily learn about and improve.
Counseling for senior living is very close to the firm's eldercare base and likely supports client acquisition across other services, so management would be strongly inclined to retain it.

The retail shop is related to sheltered-workshop activities and inclusion goals but sits farther from the firm's main care competencies, so it has the highest chance of being dropped even though it would likely be kept for now.
